diagrams.title: **One front door, many backends
diagrams.caption: **One front door, many backends.** The agent sees a single list of MCP tools; the gateway knows which backend each one calls.

diagrams.title: **Every operation becomes a tool
diagrams.caption: **Every operation becomes a tool.** Tool names follow `<TargetName>___<operationId>` (three underscores), so tools from different targets never clash.

diagrams.title: **Search first, then call
diagrams.caption: **Search first, then call.** The agent loads a short list instead of 200 definitions: fewer tokens per request and better tool choices.

diagrams.title: **Two different keys for two different doors
diagrams.caption: **Two different keys for two different doors.** Auditors in regulated industries check exactly this separation.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 340" aria-label="Inbound and outbound authentication. Inbound: the agent proves it may use the gateway with either IAM, the simple path for agents already running on AWS with an IAM role, or a JWT from Cognito, Okta or any OAuth 2.0 provider when end-user identity must flow through. Outbound, configured per target: the internal customer API gets an OAuth token, the third-party weather service gets an API key, and a Lambda target is called with the gateway's own IAM role. Credentials are stored securely, tokens are refreshed and cached. The inbound and outbound tokens are completely separate, so a downstream API cannot reuse the inbound token to impersonate the agent." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah-data" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah-data" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker><marker id="ah-tool" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah-tool" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker></defs>
        <rect x="20" y="110" width="200" height="110" rx="18" class="agent" style="fill:#19203F;stroke:#19203F;stroke-width:2"></rect><text x="120" y="172" text-anchor="middle" class="t on-agent" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#F2F4F8;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">Agent</text>
        <path d="M224 165 H376" class="ln-data" stroke-width="4" marker-end="url(#ah-data)" style="stroke:#2958C4;stroke-width:3;fill:none"></path>
        <rect x="236" y="70" width="128" height="34" rx="17" class="data" style="fill:#E1E9FC;stroke:#2958C4;stroke-width:2.5"></rect><text x="300" y="93" text-anchor="middle" class="lab" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#3A4266;font-size:15px;font-weight:700">token A</text>
        <text x="300" y="200" text-anchor="middle" class="lab ink-data" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#1C3F8F;font-size:15px;font-weight:700">INBOUND</text><text x="300" y="222" text-anchor="middle" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">IAM or JWT</text>
        <rect x="380" y="60" width="240" height="210" rx="22" class="proto" style="fill:#ECE5FC;stroke:#6C43CC;stroke-width:2.5"></rect><text x="500" y="150" text-anchor="middle" class="tl" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:24px;font-weight:700">Gateway</text><text x="500" y="180" text-anchor="middle" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">keeps A and B apart</text>
        <text x="740" y="40" text-anchor="middle" class="lab ink-tool" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#075A51;font-size:15px;font-weight:700">OUTBOUND, per target</text>
        <path d="M624 110 H856" class="ln-tool" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah-tool)" style="stroke:#0B7F73;stroke-width:3;fill:none"></path><rect x="660" y="92" width="160" height="34" rx="17" class="tool" style="fill:#D6F2EE;stroke:#0B7F73;stroke-width:2.5"></rect><text x="740" y="115" text-anchor="middle" class="lab" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#3A4266;font-size:15px;font-weight:700">OAuth token B1</text>

        <rect x="860" y="84" width="220" height="52" rx="12" class="bx" style="fill:#FFFFFF;stroke:#D7DCE8;stroke-width:2"></rect><text x="876" y="116" class="tm" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#3A4266;font-size:16px">Internal customer API</text>

      </svg>

diagrams.title: **Who's calling, and on whose behalf the agent acts
diagrams.caption: **Who's calling, and on whose behalf the agent acts.** Identity keeps those two facts connected.

<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 380" aria-label="AgentCore Identity handles both sides. diagrams.title: **Many agents need both at once
diagrams.caption: **Many agents need both at once:** user-delegated access for personal data and machine-to-machine access for shared resources.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 340" aria-label="Two OAuth flows. User-delegated access, the authorisation code grant: to read a user's own Google Calendar, the user clicks Allow once in a browser; Identity stores the resulting tokens, refreshes them when they expire, and the agent can access that user's data later without asking again. Machine-to-machine access, the client credentials grant: to reach a shared knowledge base or data warehouse where no specific user is involved, the agent authenticates as itself. Many agents need both at once." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah-data" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah-data" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker><marker id="ah-tool" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah-tool" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker></defs>
